newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown outlines job summit plans.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown outlines job summit plans.

text.p: Employability -- ensuring people have the skills to get and keep jobs -- will be the focus of a special conference in Britain next year, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Thursday.
"Employability is the key to a cohesive society which offers opportunity to all its citizens," Brown, who will host the meeting, said in a statement.

"Better education and higher skills, combined with reduced burdens on business, are the way to guarantee the high and stable levels of growth and employment which are the core goals of our economic policy," he said.

Finance and social affairs ministers from all the major industrialised countries and Russia will be invited to a summit in London next January ahead of the Group of Seven's main summit in the Midlands city of Birmingham in the summer.

They will swap ideas on how to give people the skills they need in the flexible labour markets of the future, ensuring the tax and benefit systems promote work over dependency and removing barriers to job creation, the Treasury said.

Earlier, U.S. President Bill Clinton and British Prime Minister Tony Blair announced a planned joint initiative under the umbrella of the G7, now effectively the Group of Eight with Russia's involvement, to tackle unemployment.

Speaking in the gardens of No. 10 Downing Street in London, Blair's official residence, the two leaders said they would ask other G7 members at next month's summit in Denver to launch a two-year plan aimed at reducing joblessness in the main industrial countries by increasing labour market flexibility.

Britain will take over the rotating chairmanship of the G7 after the United States. Both countries believe the rest of the G7 -- Japan, France, Germany, Italy, Canada -- can learn from their success in creating jobs by keeping labour costs low and cutting red tape to encourage small firms, officials said.
"This is the new economic agenda. It enables us to benefit from flexible labour markets, while ensuring that everyone can share in the rewards of a more dynamic economy," Brown said.
"We intend to make this a key theme of both our Presidency of the G8 and of the European Union." Britain takes over the EU presidency for the first half of 1998.
